content: Marijuana intoxication, also referred to as cannabis intoxication, occurs when an individual experiences the effects of marijuana use. These effects can include feelings of euphoria, relaxation, and, in some cases, undesirable or harmful side effects. Marijuana, commonly known by names such as pot, weed, grass, or Mary Jane, is the most widely used illicit drug in the United States. It is typically consumed by smoking, though it can also be ingested orally. Currently, there are over 12 million marijuana users in the United States and more than 300 million regular users globally. Symptoms of Marijuana Intoxication The effects of marijuana intoxication can vary depending on the method of consumption and the dose. Common effects include relaxation, drowsiness, and mild euphoria, often referred to as getting high. When marijuana is smoked, the onset of symptoms is rapid and predictable. However, when marijuana is consumed orally, the effects may take longer to appear and can be less predictable. Undesirable side effects of marijuana use tend to increase with higher doses. These side effects may include: Impaired short-term memory Dry mouth Reduced perception and motor coordination Red or bloodshot eyes In some cases, more severe side effects can occur, particularly in new users or individuals with pre-existing psychiatric conditions. These may include: Panic attacks Paranoia Acute psychosis The severity and type of side effects can vary significantly between individuals and depend on the amount of marijuana consumed. Additionally, marijuana is sometimes adulterated with other substances, such as hallucinogens or more dangerous drugs, which can lead to more serious complications. These complications may include: If the person is not breathing or has no detectable pulse, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) should be initiated and continued until emergency medical personnel arrive. Treatment Options The management of marijuana intoxication primarily involves ensuring the safety of the individual and addressing any psychological distress, such as panic or agitation. For individuals experiencing severe agitation, sedative medications such as benzodiazepines (e.g., diazepam or lorazepam) may be administered. In cases where children or individuals exhibit more serious symptoms, hospitalization may be required for close monitoring and treatment. Patients with severe complications, such as cardiac or neurological symptoms, may need specialized care, including heart or brain monitoring and the administration of appropriate medications. Prognosis The prognosis for individuals experiencing marijuana intoxication is generally favorable. However, in rare cases, severe complications such as seizures, cardiac arrest, or heart attacks can occur, which may result in fatal outcomes. These severe reactions are uncommon. For further assistance, individuals can seek medical care at hospitals equipped to treat marijuana intoxication.
